---
name: gift-ideas
description: Suggest gifts or ways to celebrate for a person and an occasion - a birthday, anniversary, wedding, new baby, Christmas, Eid, Mother's Day, a thank-you, a farewell, a host gift - from the person's interests, age, relationship and the user's budget, as a short ranked list with why each fits, plus a short card text if asked.
---
# Gift ideas

Use this when the user asks "what should I get for", "gift for my", "ideas for a present", "how to celebrate", "something small for my host", "a last-minute gift", or wants a card text.

Steps:
1. Take the facts: who (relationship, age, gender if given), the occasion, the budget (ask or use the default ranges), the person's interests and dislikes, what the user gave before, the time left (same day, a week, a month).
2. Give 6 to 8 ideas, ranked, best first. Each idea: the gift in 2 to 6 words, the rough price band, one line on why it fits this person, and a practical note (needs size, needs a booking, can be bought today, make it yourself in 1 hour).
3. Mix the kinds: one experience (a course, a ticket, a day out), one useful upgrade of something they use daily, one consumable (food, tea, a plant), one personal or hand-made thing (a photo book, a letter, a playlist), one small plus-one to add to any gift.
4. Say which one you would pick and why, in one line.
5. If asked for a card text: 2 to 4 sentences in the user's voice, with the person's name, one memory or specific trait, one wish for the occasion; formal or warm as the relationship needs; no rhyme unless asked.
6. For a group gift or a wedding: the usual forms (a shared voucher, a contribution to a trip, money in a card where that is the custom), and the one line to write with it.

Defaults:
- Budget bands if not given: small (under 20), middle (20 to 60), bigger (60 to 150), in the user's currency; say the bands you used.
- Cultural fit: for religious holidays follow the custom (no alcohol for Eid or for someone who does not drink; no clocks or knives where that is unlucky; flowers and chocolate are nearly always safe for a host); for a new baby, think of the parents too.
- Last-minute: things available in a supermarket, bookshop, florist or online as a voucher within hours; a hand-written letter.
- No luxury brands as the default; a gift that shows attention beats an expensive one.
- Do not invent product names, shops or prices beyond the band.

Output template:
For <person>, <occasion>, budget <band>:
1. <gift> (<band>) - <why it fits> - <note>
2. ...
My pick: <number> because ...
Card: "<2 to 4 sentences>"   (if asked)

Example:
User: "Gift for my dad, 65, likes gardening and crime novels, around 50 euros."
Good shape: 1 a pair of good secateurs with a sharpener (40 to 60) - he uses them every week - needs no size; 2 a hardback by a crime author he does not have yet (15 to 25) - ask which ones he read, or check his shelf; 3 a raised-bed seed set with rare tomatoes (15 to 30) - new this year; 4 a kneeling pad and gloves (20 to 30) - the knees at 65; 5 a day at a botanical garden with you (20 to 40) - time together; 6 a plus-one: a jar of his favourite jam. My pick: 1, a tool he will use for years, with a card.

Do:
- Tie each idea to one fact the user gave.
- Give one practical note per idea.
Don't:
- Don't list 20 generic items.
- Don't suggest things against the person's stated dislikes or customs.
- Don't invent shops or exact prices.

Before you answer, check: 6 to 8 ranked ideas with band, why and note; the kinds are mixed; a pick with a reason; cultural fit; card text if asked; user's language.
